prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the nearby foreground from the garage, street, and houses: in frame 1 the adult man is about 1–2 m ahead near centre-left, two smaller people are roughly 2–4 m farther left, and the car and garage interior lie behind them at about 3–6 m. In frame 2 the partially visible person at the right edge is within about 1 m, while the person in green is about 3–5 m ahead near centre and the road is farther beyond; in frame 3 the scooter is roughly 1–2 m in front-right, with one person partly hidden by vegetation to its left and another person partly cut off at the right edge. Across frames 3–5 the camera approaches and turns around the scooter, bringing its seat and body to within roughly 0.3–1 m and causing them to occlude much of the lower scene, while the person in green ends about 2–3 m ahead-left of the handlebars. The map makes distance ordering and the scooter's strong foreground occlusion clearer than RGB, but its absolute metric distances are uncertain, people sometimes merge with nearby surfaces, and dark sky, vegetation, and frame-edge regions appear unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies separate people, a backpack, bicycle, stop sign, skateboard, and motorcycle/scooter instances, making object boundaries and overlaps easier to distinguish than in RGB. In frame 1 it places three people across the left-to-centre region, with the largest adult in front of the car and the two smaller figures to his left; the backpack overlaps one smaller person, and the bicycle is only partly visible between people. In frames 2–3 it isolates the distant person near centre, another person partly entering from an edge, and the scooter in the right foreground, showing that the scooter lies in front of background people and vegetation; by frames 4–5 the large scooter mask fills much of the lower-right view while people are cropped along the top or side edges. The masks support left/right and occlusion relationships but not reliable metre-scale distance or facing direction, and they miss most background geometry, fragment some people, confuse or incompletely label small objects, and label the scooter broadly as a motorcycle.
descriptions.pose: The pose map gives body orientation for the clearest standing people: in frame 1 the large adult about 1–2 m ahead has a mostly frontal or three-quarter torso with one arm extended to the right, while a smaller figure at far left is side-on and partly cropped. In frame 2 the person near centre, roughly 3–5 m away, has a narrow side-facing skeleton with the legs angled across the walkway, indicating movement across the view rather than directly toward or away from the camera; head keypoints are too sparse to establish gaze reliably. Later frames contain no dependable full-body skeletons even though RGB and segmentation show people and the nearby scooter, so arm's-reach relations are only clear in frame 1, where the adult's extended hand is near the car, and not for the camera wearer. The skeletons reveal limb configuration and facing more clearly than RGB where bodies overlap the garage scene, but missing joints, isolated points, absent detections, and the lack of visible magenta hand skeletons make distance, gaze, occlusion, and frame-to-frame turning unreliable.
